 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1. The claimants are in appeal challenging not only exoneration of the insurer from the liability but also seek for enhancement of compensation.

2. It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 28.10.2015, K.
R. Mallikarjuna, a 63 year old died.
3. The Tribunal has recorded the finding that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger and the driver of the offending lorry did not possess the valid and effect driving license at all.
Therefore, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the insurer would have to be exonerated.

4. In light of the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of New India Assurance Co.Ltd Vs. Yallava and Ors - ILR 202 KAR 223, since the insurer was fundamentally contending that there was a breach of policy condition, the only remedy available to the insurer would be to satisfy the compensation and thereafter, to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

In this view of the matter, the finding of the Tribunal exonerating the insurer from the liability is set aside and it is held that the insurer would be liable to pay the compensation and thereafter, to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

6. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence adduced before it, has come to the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident which has resulted in the death of K. R. Mallikarjuna.

The Tribunal has thereafter proceeded to award the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 4,47,972  2. Loss of Consortium 1,00,000  3.
Funeral expenses & obsequies 10,000  4. Transportation of dead body 5,000  Total 5,62,972 7.

In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.8,000/-.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
8.
Since there are three dependents, it would be appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and his monthly income would be Rs.6,000/-.

9. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.6,000/-
10.
As the deceased was aged 63 years, a multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.5,04,000/- (6,000 x 12 x 7) towards "loss of dependency".

11. The claimants being the wife and children of the deceased, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.1,32,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

12. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:

3  Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 5,04,000
2 . Loss of Consortium 1,32,000
3. Conventional Heads 33,000  Total 6,69,000 13.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.6,69,000/- as against Rs.5,62,972/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
14.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and thereafter, to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
15. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
16. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
17. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
